**Claude finished @falvaradorodriguez's task in 3m 38s** —— [View job](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/actions/runs/32867401907)

---
### Review

Read the entitlements service, guards, filter, error, spaces repository/service/controller, and specs. This is a well-thought-out change; the transaction ownership + advisory lock + prepared quota check split is a genuinely nice shape. A few things worth improving:

#### 1. Guard does a redundant DB round-trip + live count on every gated POST

`SafeSeatsGuard.canActivate` runs **before** `SpaceIdPipe`, so both perform a lookup by UUID:

- guard: `spacesRepository.findIdByUuid(spaceUuid)` — [`entitlement.guard.ts:36`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/e27616f6cd7792b65596387d77d7859ed9d9d148/src/modules/entitlements/routes/guards/entitlement.guard.ts#L36)
- pipe: same lookup a moment later inside `@Param('spaceId', SpaceIdPipe)`

Then `assertWithinQuota({ delta: 0 })` triggers a live `countBySpaceId` (via `stockCounters.safe_seats`) — a query the repository will run **again** inside its locked transaction. So the golden-path `POST /v1/spaces/:spaceId/safes` under a plan does: 2× space lookup + 2× seat count + the actual insert. Two of those four are the guard being defensive about "already at limit" before the payload is parsed. Consider either (a) letting the pipe run first and reading the numeric id off the request in the guard, or (b) accepting that the write already gates and rejecting from the guard only on **cached** grant evidence (skip the live count).

#### 2. `admit(delta: 0)` silently means "consume 1"

[`entitlements.service.ts:186`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/e27616f6cd7792b65596387d77d7859ed9d9d148/src/modules/entitlements/routes/entitlements.service.ts#L186) does `Math.max(args.delta, 1)`. That's what makes the guard's "am I at the limit?" call reject when `used === quota`, which is correct — but it's non-obvious that `delta: 0` reports over-limit-by-one. The `IEntitlementEnforcement` doc string [notes the intent](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/e27616f6cd7792b65596387d77d7859ed9d9d148/src/modules/entitlements/domain/entitlement-enforcement.interface.ts#L11), but a `used >= grant.quota` check would say what it means without the `max(delta, 1)` sleight of hand.

#### 3. Cache-vs-materialization race can leave stale grants for up to TTL

In `materializeUnderLock` ([`entitlements.service.ts:569-573`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/e27616f6cd7792b65596387d77d7859ed9d9d148/src/modules/entitlements/routes/entitlements.service.ts#L569)) the cache is deleted **after** commit. A concurrent reader that missed the cache **before** the commit, computed old grants, and writes them back **after** the delete will re-poison the cache with the pre-materialization value for the full 5-min TTL. In practice this window is small and the PR body accepts a similar Free-tier lag, but it's a race that outlasts any single request; worth either a comment acknowledging it or a versioned key (e.g. include `lastEventAt` in the cache-dir suffix so a stale writer's key is orphaned).

#### 4. `EntitlementGuard.canActivate` — schema `catch(undefined)` + `as UUID` is fragile

[`space-id-param.schema.ts:16-19`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/e27616f6cd7792b65596387d77d7859ed9d9d148/src/modules/entitlements/routes/guards/space-id-param.schema.ts#L16) uses `.catch(undefined)` to defer everything to `SpaceIdPipe`, then narrows with `as UUID | undefined`. This depends on `UUID_REGEX` in `@/domain/common/constants` staying looser than or equal to the pipe's own validation. If someone tightens the guard schema and forgets the pipe (or vice versa), the guard silently starts admitting requests that the pipe then rejects — the current tests cover the lax case, but there's no assertion that guard vs pipe stay in sync. A one-liner test in `entitlement.guard.spec.ts` importing `UUID_REGEX` and re-checking against `SpaceIdPipe`'s validator would prevent that drift.

#### 5. Minor: `EntitlementsService` constructor is up to 13 injections

[`entitlements.service.ts:73-95`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/e27616f6cd7792b65596387d77d7859ed9d9d148/src/modules/entitlements/routes/entitlements.service.ts#L73) — the class now does resolve, cache, materialize, and enforce. That's within tolerance for now, but if a third gated feature lands here (per the follow-up in the PR description), splitting the enforcement path (`assertWithinQuota` / `prepareQuotaCheck` / `resolveGrant`) into its own `EntitlementEnforcementService` would keep this from becoming a god-service. Not a blocker for this PR.

#### 6. Nit: `preEnforcementQuotas` returns a closure per lookup

[`entitlements.service.ts:240-242`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/e27616f6cd7792b65596387d77d7859ed9d9d148/src/modules/entitlements/routes/entitlements.service.ts#L240): `Record<FeatureKey, () => number>` with `() => this.maxSafesPerSpace` is exhaustive by type, which is nice, but the closure only exists because the value is captured off `this`. A plain `Record<FeatureKey, number>` initialised in the constructor (`{ safe_seats: this.maxSafesPerSpace }`) would be equivalently exhaustive and clearer to read — the "goes away after the date" comment supports keeping it minimal, not making it callable.

#### Nothing critical

The concurrent-additions integration test at [`space-safes.repository.integration.spec.ts:416`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/e27616f6cd7792b65596387d77d7859ed9d9d148/src/modules/spaces/domain/safes/space-safes.repository.integration.spec.ts#L416) is exactly the right proof-of-life for the lock — it fails without the advisory lock and passes with it, and the assertion is on the *observable* count, not the mechanism. Nice.
